ruling.question: What does '1 cup corn' mean in this catalogue?
ruling.answer: DRAINED KERNELS. One cup = 164 g drained solids (FDC 169214), one 15.25 oz can yields 298 g drained (FDC 169214 portion '1 can (303 x 406)'), and every corn gram in a spec is a drained gram.
ruling.why: It is the encoding the catalogue already uses for every other canned item a recipe drains (all 63 non-corn, non-pineapple 'N cans' lines are drained grams; densities.can is a drained yield with the literal note 'drained grams per 15oz can'; Chickpeas / Kidney / Cannellini macro rows are FDC 'canned, drained solids'); the engine already implements it (cost-recipes.ps1 DRAINED branch); densities.cup for corn is ALREADY the drained cup; and 17 of 34 corn lines were authored on it. The other 17 are internally consistent but on the wrong side of the catalogue's own convention.
ruling.single_encoding: densities.items.'Sweet Whole Kernel Corn'.can = 298 (cited), which is < 432 x 0.95 = 410.4 and therefore admits corn to $DRAINED with no engine change; the food-DB row moves to the FDC 169214 drained-solids basis per 100 g (the Chickpeas precedent); the 17 gross lines are re-expressed to drained grams (g x 298/432, rounded) so the drained engine reads them right; the 17 cup lines keep their grams.

what_the_other_two_break.separate_drained_macro_row: A second item name for one SKU. audit-store-integrity Test-MissingSide fires HARD on a macro row with no ingredients.json row, so it needs a second price row or an alias too; a duplicate NAME is two seeding paths (orphan-name memory); the shop-this-recipe list prints two corn lines when a recipe has both; and it fixes nothing on BUY - the 17 drained lines still divide by 432 unless that row also gets a drained can, at which point it is this plan plus an extra row and a permanent two-basis item.

items.root_cause: The drained basis is not a declared property of an ingredient; it is INFERRED at cost-recipes.ps1:141 from densities.can being at least 5% below buy_pkg_g. Those are meant to be one can on two bases (drained vs net), so a row that copies the net weight into densities.can (corn 432/432, Pineapple Chunks 567/567) opts out of the drained branch silently, and nothing compares a spec line's basis ('cups, drained' at the USDA 164 g cup) with the row's basis. Writers therefore followed their sources: 17 lines drained, 17 lines gross, one item. The only guard on this seam, audit-store-integrity section 3 BASE-DRIFT (densities cup vs food-DB serving), skips every row with serving_qty != 1 (line 265), and '1/2 cup (125 g)' with serving_qty 0.5 is the shape of every Great Value canned-vegetable label row, so the 165-vs-250 g/cup split has been invisible since the row was written. bid-decisions-2026-07-26.json:51 named the drained-can basis as 'a separate calibration issue' and it was never closed.

root_fix.what: Make the basis VISIBLE and GUARDED rather than inferred: (a) BASE-DRIFT normalises the food-DB serving by serving_qty as well as by the label sentence, so the canned-label class is no longer skipped; (b) a new HARD predicate in audit-store-integrity: a spec line whose buy text says 'drained' on an item whose densities.can is not below 0.95 x buy_pkg_g is a basis contradiction (the recipe drains what the engine buys gross).
root_fix.exact_change: (a) section 3, line 265: replace `if([double]$row.serving_qty -ne 1){ continue }` with: $labelQty = Get-LabelUnitQty ([string]$row.serving_unit) $u; if($null -eq $labelQty -or $labelQty -le 0){ continue }; $sq = [double]$row.serving_qty; if($sq -le 0){ $sq = 1 }; $qty = $sq * $labelQty; $dbPerUnit = [double]$row.serving_grams / $qty. Measured: 0 rows carry both encodings, so the product is never double-applied. Keep BASE-DRIFT at WARN (its 5% band is still rounding-noise territory for most rows). (b) new function Test-DrainedLineWithoutYield { param([string]$BuyText,[double]$CanG,[double]$PkgG) return ($BuyText -match '(?<!un)\bdrained\b' -and $PkgG -gt 0 -and -not ($CanG -gt 0 -and $CanG -lt $PkgG * 0.95)) } wired into the spec loop (section 4 already walks db\recipes\*.json) as a HARD finding: 'DRAINED-NO-YIELD: <slug> :: <item> :: line says drained but densities.can <can> is not a drained yield against buy_pkg_g <pkg>'. items.deviation:
Shipped, with four recorded deviations. Every one of the plan's 34 cell_effects reproduced EXACTLY (measured before the edit and again after: street-corn 596.9->599.3, turkey-taco-soup 617.0->606.0, pastel-de-choclo 582.9->566.1, arroz 700.2->687.3, and so on for all 34), all 13 predicted +1-can buy corrections landed, and no bounded claim or cal_floor flipped. 

[1] SHIP_SEQUENCE STEP 2 DOES NOT APPLY AS WRITTEN - the '10 pre-drifted specs' is 3, and no food-DB row moved under them. The plan (and its do_not_touch line) assumed rebase-spec-ingredient -Restat enforces a 1-unit reproduce check. It does not: the -Restat tolerance is 5.0 cal / 2.0 g, deliberately matched to build-v2-spec.ps1:335-336's build gate (see that script's 2026-08-27 note). Measured against the real tolerance, only THREE of the 34 are refused - ground-turkey-calabacitas-skillet, slow-cooker-pulled-pork-bowl and tex-mex-beef-rice-skillet-bowls - and all three on CARBS (+2.03, +2.33, +2.18 against a 2.0 bar), not on calories. The plan's remedy (find which food-DB row moved under each) does not fit them: the identical drift reproduces against EVERY committed food-macros-db.json snapshot back to 2026-08-24 (18 snapshots tested), and neither their grams nor their stat has changed since 2026-08-20. Their stored stat has simply never matched a recompute of their own ingredients_grams. That is a pre-existing certification failure in 3 specs, exactly the 'fixed on its own commit, not a tolerance to widen' item the plan's do_not_touch names. NOT widened, NOT hand-written. Those 3 ship their corrected COST and BUY lines (the reader-facing under-buy is fixed on all 34) and keep their stat; their drift moves from -3.5/-0.4/+4.6 cal to -9.0/+1.4/+5.4. Named for a separate commit.

[2] THE RESTAT PROOF NEEDED THE PRIOR GRAMS, NOT JUST THE PRIOR FOOD DB. Ship_sequence step 5 re-grams 17 specs and step 7 then restats them with -PriorFoodDb; that sequence cannot work, because -Restat proves it understands a spec by recomputing the STORED stat from the prior snapshot, and after a re-gram it is reading NEW grams out of a spec whose stat was written from OLD ones. Measured: turkey-taco-soup reproduces 604.7 against a stored 619 and is refused, and so are the other 16. rebase-spec-ingredient.ps1 gained -PriorSpecDir: the proof reads prior grams + prior DB, which is the SAME safety argument evaluated against a complete snapshot instead of half of one. It is checked, not assumed - the prior file must be the same slug, the same servings and the same ingredient list, so only GRAMS may differ. Six frozen fixtures ship with it (including a must-fire on a prior file for a different recipe, and a clean twin proving a food-DB-only restat with no -PriorSpecDir behaves exactly as before). 31 of 34 specs restated through it, every one landing on the plan's predicted figure.

[3] THE NEW DRAINED-NO-YIELD PREDICATE FOUND TWO CASES THE PLAN DID NOT MEASURE, and one of them was a false positive the plan's exact_change would have shipped. Run over live data before the corn data moved, the predicate fired 9 HARD: the 6 expected corn lines, the expected chicken-al-pastor-burrito Pineapple Chunks (corn03), and TWO more. (a) mediterranean-chicken-w-marinade :: Black Olives - a FALSE POSITIVE. Its buy_pkg_g 170 is labelled '6oz drained-weight can', so the package IS a drained weight and 728 g of drained olives over a drained package is correct arithmetic. A false HARD here is not cosmetic: wave-publish P5 hard-fails on any non-zero exit from this guard, so it would have blocked every wave. The predicate now takes the buy_pkg_label and reads the estate's own declaration; it never infers one. Measured over all 351 ingredient rows, exactly one declares a drained package and exactly one declares a gross one. Two frozen fixtures added: the real Black Olives row must stay silent, and the SAME line against a package NOT declared drained must still fire, so the exemption is the declaration and nothing else. (b) creamy-tuscan-chicken-skillet :: Sun-Dried Tomatoes (Oil-Packed) - a TRUE POSITIVE and a new instance of the same class: buy_pkg_g 680 carries Brad's own note 'GROSS jar weight incl. packing oil (2026-08-16). Do not correct to drained weight - that would be a guess', while the spec asks for 193 g '1 3/4 cups oil-packed, drained'. Frozen as a must-fire fixture. It is left OPEN, because the only honest fix is a drained yield nobody has measured and Brad has already ruled that guessing it is not allowed. So after this change audit-store-integrity exits 1 on TWO HARD findings - pineapple (corn03) and the oil-packed tomatoes - both real, neither weakened.

[4] THE GOLDEN FROZEN LANE DID NOT GO RED, and the plan said it would. It reads its OWN frozen copies of densities.json and db\recipes (engine\regression-inputs\golden\inputs\), so a live densities or spec edit cannot reach it; only an ENGINE change can, which is the whole point of that lane. Verified by running it: the frozen corn row there still reads can 432 and the frozen chili-cornbread-casserole still carries 757 g. The fixture was therefore NOT re-seeded - re-seeding it would have been the exact 'regenerating fixture inputs from live data' mistake seed-golden-fixture.ps1's own header warns against.

MEASURED OUTCOME BANDS. Buy: exactly the 13 predicted cup lines gained one can (street-corn 3->4, six 2->3, six 1->2); the 17 re-grammed gross lines kept their count; crack-chicken-chili and the three 500 g lines held at 2. Macros: cup lines +0.8 to +2.5 cal (the plan's band said +0.8 to +2.4; the endpoint values are identical to its own cell_effects table, street-corn 596.9 -> 599.3, so the 2.4 was the band label rounded from rounded endpoints, not a different outcome), re-grammed lines -1.6 to -16.8 cal exactly as stated. Claims: street-corn 599.3 (the literal 'under 600' was replaced by the {{cal}} token per corn02), green-chile-chicken-burrito 389.1 under 400, both cal_floors hold. Cost: 33 of the 34 moved at most +$0.050 per serving, inside the plan's $0.06 band. The one exception is street-corn at +$0.080, and it decomposes cleanly: +$0.052 is corn (util 1.62 -> 2.35 over 14 servings, in band) and the rest is the deliberate lime rebid from queue item 2026-09-02-street-corn-lime, not this item.

items.subject: Brad: street-corn-chicken-rice-bowls keeps 'under 600 calories' by 0.7 cal after the corn basis fix (599.3); is sub-1-calorie headroom acceptable on a printed bounded claim, and is DRAINED the catalogue-wide meaning of a canned-vegetable cup?

items.root_cause: A bounded claim written as a literal has no margin policy; the estate has no rule for how much headroom a printed 'under N' must carry, so a 0.7 cal survival is technically compliant and practically fragile.

items.premise_verified: TRUE. The two literals were still in place and are the only ones in the catalogue within 5 cal of their bound: intro_html read 'stays under 600 calories' and head.description read 'under 600 calories each', both alongside a {{protein}} token, and stat.cal was 597 before the corn re-basis and 599 after.
